phishingTest.explanation: Not phishing-resistant: a code captured by a simulated attacker proxy and relayed to the genuine server within its validity window was accepted, because the code carries no origin binding.

replayTest.explanation: Replay rejected: the server advanced its counter past the matched value, so the same code no longer falls inside the look-ahead window.

desynchronisationObservation.explanation: A token 2 presses ahead was accepted and the server resynchronised (counter → 3); a token 3 presses ahead fell outside the look-ahead window and was rejected. Counter desynchronisation beyond the window needs manual resynchronisation (Chapter 2 §2.4.1.3).

bruteForceTest.explanation: After 5 wrong guesses the credential was locked, and the correct code was refused afterwards. An online guesser has at most 5 tries × 3 acceptable value(s) out of 10^6, a success probability of about 1.50e-5 per lockout period.

expiredCodeTest.explanation: HOTP codes have no time-based expiry. An unused code generated 24 h earlier was still accepted; a captured but unused HOTP code stays valid until a later code is used.

securityNotes: Controlled simulations of defined attack scenarios against this implementation; not penetration testing and not a discovery of unknown vulnerabilities.

phishingTest.explanation: Not phishing-resistant: a code captured by a simulated attacker proxy and relayed to the genuine server within its validity window was accepted, because the code carries no origin binding.

replayTest.explanation: Replay rejected: the code was marked used on first successful verification.

desynchronisationObservation.explanation: No shared counter or clock: each code is generated by the server per transaction and governed only by its expiry timestamp.

bruteForceTest.explanation: After 5 wrong guesses the challenge was invalidated, and the correct code was refused afterwards. An online guesser has at most 5 tries × 1 acceptable value(s) out of 10^6, a success probability of about 5.00e-6 per lockout period.

expiredCodeTest.explanation: A code submitted 301 s after issue (expiry 300 s) was rejected (expired).

securityNotes: Controlled simulations of defined attack scenarios against this implementation; not penetration testing and not a discovery of unknown vulnerabilities.
Email-account compromise and SMTP-hop interception (Chapter 2 §2.4.3.2) are not simulated; real providers are forced to use TLS (requireTLS).
